'''Darrun Cordell Hilliard II''' (born April 13, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].

Hilliard attended [[Liberty High School (Bethlehem, Pennsylvania)|Liberty High School]] in [[Bethlehem, Pennsylvania]], where he was a two-time ''[[Associated Press]]'' first-team selection. As a high school senior, he averaged 19.7 points per game. Hilliard committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]] and coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]]. He showed steady improvement every year, going from 4.8 points per game as a freshman to 14.3 points per game as a senior as he helped Villanova reach the NCAA Tournament in three straight seasons. As a senior, he was named to the first-team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] and was honored as [[Robert V. Geasey Trophy|Big 5 Player of the Year]].

==Early life==
Hilliard was born on April 13, 1993, to Charlene Jenkins and Darrun Hilliard.<ref name=Villanova>{{cite web|title=4 – Darrun Hilliard|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/darrun_hilliard_760838.html|website=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|publisher=[[Villanova University]]|access-date=December 23, 2014|archive-date=September 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918013721/http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/darrun_hilliard_760838.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> His mother is a representative for an insurance company.<ref name="Mothers">{{cite news |last=Smallwood |first=John |date=May 11, 2013 |title=Villanova's Hilliard thinks every day should be Mother's Day |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/20130512_Villanova_s_Hilliard_thinks_every_day_should_be_Mother_s_Day.html |access-date=September 14, 2023}}</ref> His father played basketball at the high school level and first introduced his son to the sport when he was five years old. Growing up, Hilliard also played football, but preferred basketball.<ref name=ExpressTimes>{{cite news|last=Hinkel|first=Tom|title=Liberty High School's Darrun Hilliard repeats as Boys Basketball Player of the Year|url=https://www.lehighvalleylive.com/sports/index.ssf/2011/03/liberty_high_schools_darrun_hi.html|access-date=December 23, 2014|work=[[The Express-Times]]|date=March 29, 2011}}</ref> His favorite [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] player was [[Allen Iverson]].<ref name=careerday/> He used to bike to [[Philadelphia Eagles]] practices as a kid.<ref name=saved>{{cite news|last=Frank|first=Reuben|title=Darrun Hilliard on Villanova teammates: 'They saved my life'|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/ncaa/darrun-hilliard-villanova-teammates-they-saved-my-life|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[Comcast SportsNet]]|date=March 23, 2015}}</ref>

==High school career==
Hilliard attended [[Liberty High School (Bethlehem, Pennsylvania)|Liberty High School]] in [[Bethlehem, Pennsylvania]], where he was a two-time ''[[Associated Press]]'' first-team selection.<ref name=Mothers/> Despite eating, writing, and throwing a football right handed, Hilliard shoots left-handed. As a freshman, he measured {{Convert|6|ft|1|in}}. His parents split up after his freshman year, and he developed a unique bond with Liberty assistant coach Mike Bachman.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jones |first=David |date=February 24, 2014 |title=Darrun Hilliard is Villanova's hidden engine in its 24–3 season |website=pennlive.com |url=https://www.pennlive.com/sports/2014/02/darrun_hilliard_is_villanovas.html |access-date=September 14, 2023}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 18 points and six rebounds per game and shot 52 percent from the field. Hilliard led the Hurricanes to [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association|PIAA]] state semifinals, where Liberty lost to [[Penn Wood High School|Penn Wood]]. In the loss to Penn Wood, Hilliard had 26 points. He was named ''[[The Morning Call]]'' player of the year as a junior.<ref name="Groller">{{cite news |last=Groller |first=Keith |date=April 2, 2010 |title=Liberty's Darrun Hilliard is The Morning Call's boys player of the year |work=[[The Morning Call]] |url=https://www.mcall.com/2010/04/02/libertys-darrun-hilliard-is-the-morning-calls-boys-player-of-the-year |access-date=September 14, 2023}}</ref> In addition, he was selected to the First Team Class AAAA.<ref>{{cite news|title=Liberty High School's Darrun Hilliard named first team all-state; Chad Landis is Class AAAA co-coach of the year|url=https://www.lehighvalleylive.com/sports/index.ssf/2010/04/post_48.html|access-date=December 23, 2014|work=[[The Express-Times]]|date=April 7, 2010}}</ref>

Hilliard averaged 19.7 points per game as a senior.<ref name=Villanova/> He was named ''[[The Express-Times]]'' player of the year after leading the Hurricanes to the second round of the PIAA playoffs. Hilliard scored 1,413 points in his high school career, finishing second in Liberty High School history.<ref name=ExpressTimes/> He committed to [[Villanova University|Villanova]] in November 2010.<ref name="Emotional">{{cite news |last=Housenick |first=Tom |date=November 12, 2014 |title=It will be an emotional homecoming for Villanova's Darrun Hilliard, a Liberty High product |work=[[The Morning Call]] |url=https://www.mcall.com/2014/11/12/it-will-be-an-emotional-homecoming-for-villanovas-darrun-hilliard-a-liberty-high-product |access-date=September 14, 2023}}</ref> When Hilliard informed his mother he was receiving a full scholarship to Villanova, she did not understand and was trying to figure how much she would have to pay for her son's education.<ref name=Mothers/>

==College career==
===Freshman===
Villanova coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] considered [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] Hilliard in his freshman season, but Wright decided against it after a rash of injuries to his players.<ref name=Emotional/> He had 13 points in back-to-back games against [[2011–12 Penn Quakers men's basketball team|Penn]] and [[2011–12 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] in December 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Villanova 73, Penn 65|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=313370222|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209023537/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=313370222|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2021|access-date=June 1, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 3, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Marcus Denmon scores 28 points, leads Missouri at Jimmy V Classic|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=313400222|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119015554/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=313400222|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2019|access-date=June 1, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 7, 2011}}</ref> As a freshman, Hilliard averaged 4.8 points, 2.5 rebounds and 18.1 minutes per game in 29 games and shot 29.2 percent from behind the three-point arc. During the season, he reached out to his family and friends to see if he made the right decision to come to Villanova. He said, "Freshman year was probably my toughest year of basketball", due to difficulties in adjusting to a new coach and teammates.<ref name=Emotional/> He described himself as a mentally unstable 17-year-old.<ref name=saved/>

===Sophomore===
In his sophomore season ([[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]]), he averaged 11.4 points in just under 30 minutes a game. This proved to be his breakout season and he would go on to start all 34 games that year.<ref name=Villanova/> He helped Villanova defeat a few top-five teams that season. In a comeback win over #5 [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] on January 22, he made a three-point play after making a steal at halfcourt which helped spark the rally.<ref>{{cite news|title=Achraf Yacoubou's late 3-pointer helps Nova upset No. 5 Louisville|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330220222|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 23, 2013}}</ref> In a 75–71 overtime victory over #3 [[2012–13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] on January 26, 2013, he had 25 points and six assists in 38 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|title=Villanova uses deep touch to upend No. 3 Syracuse in overtime|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330260222|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116083150/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330260222|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 16, 2017|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 26, 2013}}</ref> As a result of his play against Syracuse, Hilliard was honored as Big East Player of the Week and Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hinkel|first=Tom|title=Former Liberty High School basketball standout Darrun Hilliard is a rising star at Villanova|url=https://www.lehighvalleylive.com/sports/index.ssf/2013/01/former_liberty_high_basketball.html|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[The Express-Times]]|date=January 30, 2013}}</ref> He also helped them beat then #5 [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] on March 6 by the score of 67–57. In that game, he had 14 points and three [[steal (basketball)|steals]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Villanova beats another top-5 team, sinks No. 5 Georgetown|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330650222|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 7, 2013}}</ref>

Villanova enjoyed a 20–14 season after a down year and reached the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they were seeded ninth and matched up with eight seed [[2012–13 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the first round. Hilliard had a strong showing in a 78–71 loss to [[2012–13 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]], scoring 18 points.<ref>{{cite news|title=UNC outlasts Villanova to give Roy Williams win No. 700|access-date=March 12, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=March 22, 2013|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330810153}}</ref>

===Junior===
Hilliard improved in most offensive categories in the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]], his junior year. He averaged 14.3 points per game that season and improved his three-point shooting percentage to 41.4 percent (up from 31.5 percent the year before). He made 70 [[three-pointers]] that year out of 169 attempts.<ref name=Villanova/> Hilliard scored 20 points on 8-of-13 shooting against [[2013–14 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] in a 94–85 victory on January 25, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 4 Villanova holds off Marquette, 94–85 in OT|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400504544|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 25, 2014}}</ref> In an 82–79 win over [[2013–14 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]], he hit a crucial 3-pointer with a minute left in overtime.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 9 Villanova survives scare, escapes Providence in 2OT|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400504575|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 19, 2014}}</ref> In a 73–56 win over Marquette on March 2 at the [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]], he established a new career high with 26 points on 7-of-11 shooting from the field.<ref name=careerday>{{cite news|title=Villanova tops Marquette on Darrun Hilliard's career day|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400504592|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 2, 2014}}</ref>

news|last=Jerardi|first=Dick|title=Villanova at a loss in tournament|url=https://www.philly.com/philly/columnists/20140324_Villanova_at_a_loss_in_tournament.html|access-date=June 3, ===Senior===
{{quote box|width=300px|align=right|qalign=right|bgcolor=#c6dbf7|quote=He is the leader of our team, on and off the court. Defensively he can guard small forwards, guards. He always hits big shots for us. Teams are leaning to him a lot more and he's creating shots for his teammates. The way he's handled everything unselfishly and done everything for the team, he's put winning first ahead of individual accomplishments. I'm thrilled that he's a candidate for player of the year and I'd love for him to get it.|source = Jay Wright<ref name=inline/>}}

Coming into the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]], Hilliard was named to the Preseason Second Team All-Big East.<ref name=bigeast/> He averaged 14.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game as a senior.<ref name=Villanova/> Villanova was ranked in the top ten for most of the season thanks to a balanced offense. Hilliard scored 23 points on December 20 in an overtime victory over [[2014–15 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]], hitting 9-of-17 shots. He hit two free throws to give the Wildcats the first lead of the game in overtime before being kicked in the face and tested for concussion-like symptoms.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 7 Villanova stays undefeated with overtime win over Syracuse|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400587863|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 20, 2014}}</ref> Against [[2014–15 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] on January 25, 2015, he scored 24 points and made 6-of-10 three-pointers in a 71–50 victory at home.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hilliard scores 24 to lead No. 4 Villanova over Creighton|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400588431|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 25, 2015}}</ref> On February 14, in a 78–75 victory over [[2014–15 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]], Hilliard scored a career-high 31 points and also set a career high with 8 three-pointers made out of 13 attempts. He also hit the game-winning three-pointer with 1.5 seconds to play in the game. Eight of his nine field goals in that game were three-pointers, and his eight rebounds were one short of a career-high.<ref>{{cite news|title=Darrun Hilliard hits clutch 3 as No. 6 Villanova rallies by No. 18 Butler|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400588458|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 26, 2015}}</ref> He averaged 18.7 points during a nine-game stretch that included the Butler game.<ref name=inline>{{cite news|last=Juliano|first=Joe|title=Hilliard in line for Big East honor|url=https://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/20150311_Hilliard_in_line_for_Big_East_honor.html|access-date=June 3, 2015|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 11, 2015}}</ref>

State]] in the NCAA Tournament Round of 32, despite contributing 27 points. ==Professional career==
===Detroit Pistons (2015–2017)===
Prior to the [[2015 NBA draft]], Hilliard signed with James Dunleavy as his agent. He was listed in the 55–70 range among NBA draft prospects by several media agencies.<ref>{{cite news|last=Miller|first=Stephen|title=Liberty High product Darrun Hilliard hopeful as NBA Draft nears|url=http://www.mcall.com/sports/varsity/mc-darrun-hilliard-nba-draft-advance-20150624-story.html|access-date=June 28, 2015|work=[[The Morning Call]]|date=June 24, 2015}}</ref> On June 25, 2015, Hilliard was selected 38th overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the second round of the draft.<ref>{{cite news|last=Farrell|first=Perry|title=Pistons take Villanova SG Darrun Hilliard 38th in NBA draft|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2015/06/25/darrun-hilliard-detroit-pistons/29316955/|access-date=June 25, 2015|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=June 25, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/villanovas-hilliard-brings-versatility-savvy-shooting-pistons-perimeter|title=Villanova's Hilliard brings versatility, savvy, Pistons|url=http://www.mcall.com/sports/mc-darrun-hilliard-draft-follow-20150626-story.html|access-date=June 28, 2015|work=[[The Morning Call]]|date=June 26, 2015}}</ref> After averaging 9.4 points per game in [[2015 NBA Summer League|Orlando Summer League]] play, on July 20, Hilliard signed a three-year deal with the Pistons, with one year being guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-second-round-pick-darrun-hilliard|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Second-Round Pick Darrun Hilliard|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=July 20, 2015|access-date=July 20, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Ellis|first=Vince|title=Pistons agree to terms with second-rounder Hilliard|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2015/07/16/detroit-pistons-darrun-hilliard/30249287/|access-date=July 17, 2015|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=July 16, 2015}}</ref> Coach [[Stan Van Gundy]] praised Hilliard's shooting prowess, despite a poor showing in the Summer League.<ref name=langlois>{{cite web|last=Langlois|first=Keith|title=Darrun Hilliard catches the eyes of not only SVG but his new Pistons teammates|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/darrun-hilliard-catches-eyes-not-only-svg-his-new-pistons-teammates|website=[[NBA.com]]|access-date=September 2, 2015|date=August 5, 2015}}</ref>

He broke his nose during training camp after engaging in a pickup game. The injury required surgery and he needed to wear a mask.<ref>{{cite news|last=McMann|first=Aaron|title=Masked Darrun Hilliard willing to stretch the floor to earn Pistons roster spot|url=https://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2015/10/masked_darrun_hilliard_willing_1.html|access-date=November 24, 2015|work=MLive|date=October 1, 2015}}</ref> On November 23, he made his NBA debut in a 109–88 loss against the [[2015–16 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]], recording two points and three rebounds in 12 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|title=Monroe helps Bucks beat Pistons 109–88|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151123/DETMIL/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|access-date=December 5, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=November 23, 2015|archive-date=November 27, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151127061231/http://www.nba.com/games/20151123/DETMIL/gameinfo.html}}</ref> During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Grand Rapids Drive]], the Pistons' [[D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015–16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=December 19, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }}</ref>

On June 30, 2016, Hilliard was ruled out of the [[2016 NBA Summer League]] after he suffered a stress fracture of the lower back.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19375|title=Darrun Hilliard suffers lower back stress fracture|work=InsideHoops.com|date=June 30, 2016|access-date=June 30, 2016}}</ref> During the 2016–17 season, Hilliard had multiple assignments with the Grand Rapids Drive.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016–17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 11, 2017|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On June 28, 2017, Hilliard was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for cash considerations,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-trade-guard/forward-darrun-hilliard-houston-rockets|title=Detroit Pistons Trade Guard/Forward Darrun Hilliard To Houston Rockets|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2017|access-date=June 28, 2017}}</ref> then immediately got traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] as part of the trade that sent [[Chris Paul]] to Houston.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-la-clippers-acquire-seven-players-and-draft-pick-including-beverley-dekker-harrell-and|title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Acquire Seven Players and Draft Pick, Including Beverley, Dekker, Harrell and Williams|last=Ibarra|first=Joseph|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2017|access-date=June 28, 2017}}</ref> A day later, he was waived by the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/darrun-hilliard-waived-by-clippers/|title=Darrun Hilliard: Waived by Clippers|work=cbssports.com|date=June 29, 2017|access-date=June 29, 2017}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2017–2018)===
On September 11, 2017, Hilliard signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], meaning he would be available to split playing time between San Antonio and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Spurs sign Darrun Hilliard to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-darrun-hilliard-two-way-contract|last=Julian|first=M.|access-date=September 11, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=September 11, 2017}}</ref> On February 23, 2018, in his first game in the G League in a month, Hilliard contributed 31 points, five assists, one rebound and one steal in a 134–123 loss to the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs' Darrun Hilliard: Erupts for 31 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-darrun-hilliard-erupts-for-31/ |access-date=June 12, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 23, 2018}}</ref> He had 22 points, four rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in a win against the [[Reno Bighorns]] on March 10. He posted 21.2 points per game for Austin.<ref>{{cite news |title=Darrun Hilliard: Scores 22 points in G League game |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/darrun-hilliard-scores-22-points-in-g-league-game/ |access-date=June 12, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 10, 2018}}</ref>

===Kirolbet Baskonia (2018–2019)===
On August 13, 2018, Hilliard signed a one-year deal with [[Saski Baskonia|Kirolbet Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Darrun Hilliard refuerza el perímetro azulgrana – Saski Baskonia |url=https://www.baskonia.com/darrun-hilliard-refuerza-el-perimetro-azulgrana/ |access-date=13 August 2018 |work=Saski Baskonia |date=13 August 2018 |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Baskonia lands perimeter help in Hilliard |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8xtdsjexackj935b |access-date=13 August 2018 |work=EuroLeague.net |date=13 August 2018}}</ref> He averaged 9.4 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.<ref name="sportando">{{cite news |title=CSKA Moscow signs Darrun Hilliard |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-signs-darrun-hilliard/ |website=Sportando |access-date=February 14, 2020 |date=July 3, 2019 |last=Carchia |first=Emiliano |archive-date=December 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209015837/https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-signs-darrun-hilliard/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===CSKA Moscow (2019–2021)===
On July 3, 2019, Hilliard signed a one-year deal with the Russian team [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref name=sportando/> He scored 14 points in a win against his former team [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] on January 17, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=James, Hilliard lead CSKA past Baskonia |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/james-hilliard-lead-cska-past-baskonia/ |website=Sportando |access-date=February 14, 2020 |date=January 17, 2020 |last=Lupo |first=Nicola |archive-date=April 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230430163354/https://sportando.basketball/en/james-hilliard-lead-cska-past-baskonia/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On June 25, 2020, Hilliard extended the contract for one year. He scored a career-high 31 points on November 11, in a win against Baskonia.<ref>{{cite news |title=Darrun Hilliard scores 31 PTS, leads CSKA to victory over Baskonia |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/darrun-hilliard-scores-31-pts-leads-cska-to-victory-over-baskonia/ |website=Sportando |access-date=November 12, 2020 |date=November 12, 2020|last=Lupo |first=Nicola }}</ref> During the 2020–21 season, he averaged 8.7 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.1 assists per game. On June 18, 2021, Hilliard parted ways with the Russian powerhouse.<ref>{{cite web |last=Tsakos |first=Alexandros |title=CSKA Moscow extends contract of Nikita Kurbanov; parts ways with Darrun Hilliard |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/129524-cska-moscow-extends-contract-of-nikita-kurbanov-parts-ways-with-darrun-hilliard |website=TalkBasket.net |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=June 18, 2021}}</ref>

===Bayern Munich (2021–2022)===
On July 16, 2021, Hilliard signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|FC Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Darrun Hilliard signs with Bayern Munich |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/darrun-hilliard-signs-with-bayern-munich/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=July 16, 2021|last=Maggi |first=Alessandro }}</ref> During the 2021–22 season, he averaged 12.7 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Darrun-Hilliard/International/28956/2022/By_Season/Per_Game/0/All_Leagues|title=Darrun Hilliard International Stats, San Antonio Spurs - RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com}}</ref>

=== Maccabi Tel Aviv (2022–2023) ===
On June 26, 2022, Hilliard signed a one-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maccabi adds veteran SG/SF Darrun Hilliard |url=http://www.maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=8989&lang=en |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=Maccabi Tel Aviv Basketball Club}}</ref>

=== Pınar Karşıyaka (2023–2024) ===
On September 1, 2023, he signed with [[Pınar Karşıyaka]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketfaul.com.tr/gundem/karsiyakadan-onemli-hamle/|title=Karşıyaka'dan önemli hamle|last=|first=|date=September 5, 2023|website=|publisher=basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=September 6, 2023}}</ref>

=== Bilbao Basket (2025–present) ===
On June 20, 2025, he signed with [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/darrun-hilliard-signs-with-bilbao/|title=Darrun Hilliard signs with Bilbao|last=|first=|date=June 20, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=June 20, 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
Hilliard played with the senior [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]], where he won a gold medal. He was named to the [[FIBA AmeriCup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]].
